from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
p=Path('tmp/pdfs');p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
alltext=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
    alltext.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(alltext))
print('\\n'.join(alltext[:3]))
PY"

strengths: NCI offers a practical, lightweight post-hoc detector using classifier weights, a stored feature mean, and feature norms. Its additional computation is O(P) once the classifier prediction is available, without storing a feature bank or retraining. Table 1b reports latency comparable to MSP: 0.54 versus 0.53 ms on CIFAR-10 and 6.84 versus 6.85 ms on ImageNet.

The evaluation covers six dataset–architecture configurations across ResNet, DenseNet, ViT, and Swin, including challenging ImageNet OOD datasets. Table 3 reports average AUROC of 88.57 versus 86.80 for Scale. The Swin improvement is particularly substantial: 80.97 versus 76.71 AUROC. These results support the usefulness of the method across varied settings.

The ablations substantiate the combination of alignment and norm information. On ImageNet ResNet-50, Table 6 improves AUROC from 84.41 for proximity alone and 78.91 for L1 alone to 88.56 for NCI, exceeding KNN plus L1 at 86.37. Tables 4 and 7 also support the chosen norm and proximity metric.
weaknesses: The central explanation for larger ID feature norms is mathematically unsupported. A simplex ETF preserves its angular structure under arbitrary positive rescaling, so maximum angular separation does not require large radii. Moreover, NC2 describes centered features, whereas the filter uses the uncentered norm ||h||1. Neural-collapse conditions do not constrain OOD feature norms either. The empirical benefit of the norm term therefore does not validate the claimed geometric explanation. Figure 2 studies one CIFAR-10/SVHN setting, and Appendix E reproduces prior results rather than measuring collapse in the evaluated checkpoints.

Theorem 3.1 overstates what its proof establishes. Equation 4 controls a normalized difference, whereas Equation 2 claims unnormalized convergence. If class-mean norms grow, vanishing directional error need not yield vanishing absolute error; additional norm or convergence-rate assumptions are required. A directional statement would support the angular score, but the theorem as written is not justified.

The methodological distinction from closely related scores needs stronger evidence. Equation 6 simplifies to pScore = (logit_c - b_c - w_c^T mu_G) / ||h - mu_G||2, a normalized, centered predicted-class logit. Comparisons with max-logit variants and norm-augmented fDBD would help establish what the proposed construction contributes beyond existing score components. Table 6 tests norm-augmented KNN but leaves these closer alternatives unresolved.

Some evaluation details prevent confidently verifying comparison parity. Section 4.1 identifies the ImageNet ResNet-50 as an OpenOOD model, while Appendix A.3 describes a default PyTorch checkpoint; this matters because many baseline results are imported from OpenOOD. The ImageNet KNN timing is also imported from another paper without establishing equivalent timing conditions. Overall, the broad empirical gains and efficiency place this near acceptance, but the unsupported central explanation and incomplete differentiation from related scores keep my recommendation at the decision boundary.
